body.text: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix: Oscar Piastri finishes third, Max Verstappen wins
Oscar Piastri has produced his finest performance of the 2026 season, claiming a sensational podium in Las Vegas after starting 17th on the grid.

Max Verstappen proved why he is one of the finest Formula 1 drivers of any era, winning a thrilling grand prix that will rank as one of the best this season. There were 352 overtakes on track, with 35 of those passes for the lead of the race.

Piastri took a 10-place grid penalty for using a new internal combustion engine, and was driving a McLaren described by team CEO Zak Brown as a "sitting duck" on the long straights, due to the car's lack of top speed.
But Piastri picked his way through the field across an action-packed 50 laps, crossing the line third behind Verstappen and McLaren teammate Lando Norris.
Piastri, who is notoriously cool under pressure, had an uncharacteristic snap at his team when they stressed the importance of being careful with his teammate Norris.
With a few laps remaining, and both drivers battling in a tightly packed top-five, Piastri was told he needed to be careful if he was battling his teammate, but Piastri was having none of it.
"Stop telling me to f****** be careful," he snapped.
Piastri would overtake Norris a few laps later, but his world champion teammate re-took the position on lap 48 of 50.
Neither McLaren driver looked set to finish on the podium, but the Mercedes duo of George Russell (off track) and Kimi Antonelli (energy deployment issue) both fell down the order.
"They say Las Vegas is the entertainment capital of the world, and I think that was pretty entertaining," Piastri said post-race.
"Everyone was just in such a big pack; it was bizarre to be a part of."
Verstappen wins after 35 lead changes
In 2025, Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix when there were 17 overtakes on track during the entire race.
In 2026, he won when there were 35 overtakes on track, just for the lead.
Verstappen was at his masterful best on Sunday (AEDT), converting pole position into the 75th grand prix win of his career.
The long straights at the Las Vegas Strip circuit resulted this year with a very powerful slipstream, meaning the car behind at the end of the straight would be going much quicker.
Verstappen drove a near-perfect race, losing the lead at the end of the long back straight several times, only to then smartly deploy his electrical power to retake the lead just a few corners later.

George Russell, Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris all overtook Verstappen for the lead at the end of the back straight at some point, only for the four-time world champion to snatch the lead straight back.
"Crazy. Really, really surreal and something I have never seen before in Formula 1 myself," Verstappen said post-race.
Verstappen was ever present in the lead, while several drivers battled to be the next challenger to the Dutchman's position.
Russell, who started second, was Verstappen's main threat throughout the race, but while running third behind his teammate Antonelli late in the race, locked his wheels and went off the track.

Antonelli was shaping up to be Verstappen's challenger on the final lap, but an energy deployment issue on the penultimate lap led to the new world champion falling behind Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli would finish fourth.

Isack Hadjar, Verstappen's teammate, looked destined to be a contender as well. However, his race came unstuck when his front wing collapsed, without contact, on lap 26 during a restart after a safety car.

Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto were fifth and sixth, a terrific result to help cement the team into sixth place in the constructors' championship, and give them an outside chance of finishing fifth.
Lewis Hamilton was seventh for Ferrari, while Carlos Sainz secured a vital eighth place for Williams.
Russell was ninth after his late mistake, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc dropped to 10th following a 10-second penalty for colliding with teammate Hamilton.

Max Verstappen speaks after winning in Vegas

Crazy. Really, really surreal and something I have never seen before in Formula 1 myself. I think in the beginning we had the deployment correct, and people were learning and watching what you were doing. We had it set up well, but crazy amount of fighting... It was impossible to drive off. Very happy with such a crazy race to come out on top.

What to know about the Las Vegas Strip circuit
The Las Vegas Strip circuit — the upside-down pig.
This street circuit is the most unique on the calendar because it opens back up to the public during the day.
It has 17 corners (although turn 13 really is just a minor turn of the wheel).
There are three straights where Straight Mode (opening the front and rear wing) is allowed.
The detection point for Overtake Mode is out of turn 16, with drivers able to use it almost immedately after for the next lap.
The corners at the end of the straight zones — turns 1, 5 and 14) offer the best overtaking opportunities for drivers.

Verstappen and Russell on the front row, after a practice squabble

I think the warning was fine. There's nothing in the rules to say that you cannot overtake someone who is starting their lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over.

Lando Norris predicts chaos in Las Vegas
Lando Norris has three races left as the reigning world champion before that honour is handed over to Mercedes star Kimi Antonelli.
But the McLaren driver is not going to spend his final days as reigning champion just going through the motions.
He has his eyes set on a big performance in Las Vegas, but has said he expects "chaos".

The long straights on this track should provide plenty of overtaking chances, while this track does not appear to be one of the strongest for battery recharge — meaning drivers will need to be very selective of when they use their electrical power because it takes a long time to charge back up.
"I think it's going to be a race full of chaos," Norris said. "It's going to be fun, it's going to be exciting, and it's going to be a long race."

But don't fear, the Victorian has a plan.

The slipstream effect down these long straights will also be a big factor today, as it was shown to be very powerful during qualifying yesterday.

I don't think tyre management will be too much of a factor, but definitely patience. It's going to be a long race; qualifying itself was pretty entertaining with trying to get a slipstream. So the race is going to be pretty exciting, I think.

Why is Oscar Piastri starting 17th in today's race
You may have noticed Oscar Piastri is starting 17th for the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, despite qualifying 7th.
The Australian has taken a 10-place grid penalty as the team gave him an upgraded power unit for this weekend.
The new power unit components exceeded the yearly allocation, meaning Piastri has to take a penalty,
To be more specific, a new internal combustion engine (ICE) has been fitted to Piastri's MCL40, while he and teammate Lando Norris are using new turbochargers this weekend.
Key Event
Catch up on yesterday's qualifying session
— reporting by Reuters

Kimi Antonelli may have already secured the world drivers' championship, but he and Mercedes proved they aren't done yet as the 20-year-old wunderkind posted the fastest qualifying time on Friday ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
However, Antonelli was denied his eighth pole of the season by a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation.

Antonelli had a time of 1 minute, 33.893 seconds, edging out Verstappen by 0.258 seconds in the closing moments of qualifying with a dramatic final lap. Mercedes sent Antonelli out for his final lap with just a second remaining in Q3, which ended up being yet another timely move for the sport's dominant team this season.

"It was very weird qualifying for me," Antonelli said. "First of all, I couldn't get the tyres working, just zero feeling with the car, and also the brake pedal was very long, so I was struggling on the braking. But all in all, it was so unexpected. And that last lap, I thought I was screwed because I started one second from the car in front, but the tow is so big here that I was able to gain with that and put it on pole."

Red Bull needs every break it can get to eclipse Ferrari for second place in the constructors' championship, and it got a couple on Friday. In addition to Verstappen ending up on the pole and Isack Hadjar qualifying in fifth, both Ferraris missed Q3 for the first time since the 2025 Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix, as Charles Leclerc qualified 11th and Lewis Hamilton qualified 12th.

"I think we had a solid qualifying," Verstappen said. "We executed well. My first lap in Q3 was pretty much as good as it can be. I think just with the tow effect as well around the lap, I think (being on) the front row is very good for us."
Mercedes' George Russell qualified third, 0.331 seconds behind Antonelli, but will start alongside Verstappen on the front row.

Lando Norris qualified fourth and Oscar Piastri qualified seventh for McLaren as last year's constructors' champions look to eclipse Red Bull for a third-place finish in the final three races. However, Piastri is facing a 10-place grid penalty for installing a fifth internal combustion engine this season, above F1's limit.
Both Racing Bulls drivers qualified in the top 10, as Arvid Lindblad had the sixth-fastest time and Liam Lawson was the eighth-fastest.
